chunks: One of our companions narrated from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from a man who was known as Rūzbih and was one of the Zaydīs, from Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī who said,

Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) said to me, ‘There is no servant who performs an action that Allah is not pleased with but that Allah initially conceals it [from the people]. If he repeats it a second time, Allah hides it [again], but if he repeats it once more, Allah sends down an angel in the form of a man to tell the people, ‘He did such and such.’”

key_terms.صُورَةِ آدَمِيٍّ: in the form of a man/human

ai.seo_question: How does Allah conceal and then reveal a servant's sins according to the hadith of Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam Abū Jaʿfar (peace be upon him) outlines a progressive divine pedagogy where Allah initially conceals a servant's minor sin out of mercy; if repeated, He continues to veil it, but upon a third repetition, He sends an angel in human form to publicly reveal the sin, serving as a humbling sign for the community. This narration, found in *Kitab al-Zuhd*, highlights the transition from private concealment (*satr*) to public exposure (*kashf*) as a mechanism for spiritual accountability. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the balance between divine mercy and the social dimension of repentance.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 14.One of our companions narrated from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from a man who was known as Rūzbih and was one of the Zaydīs, from Abū Ḥamzah al-Thumālī who said, “

Abū Jaʿfar (a) said to me, ‘There is no servant who performs an action that Allah is not pleased with but that Allah initially conceals it [from the people]. If he repeats it a second time, Allah hides it [again], but if he repeats it once more, Allah sends down an angel in the form of a man to tell the people, ‘He did such and such.’”
